term: Scope of a Variable or Function
definition: Scope refers to the visibility of variables and functions in parts of a program.
details: Scope refers to the visibility of variables and functions in parts of a program. It determines the accessibility of these variables and functions to various parts of the code.

explainer.lead: Scope is the visibility of variables and functions in parts of a program. It matters because it determines which parts of the code can access a given name.

tiers.eli5: Like rooms in a house: something kept in one room is only reachable if you are in that room or allowed in.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on scope to keep names local and avoid unintended interference between parts of a program. A pitfall is a name resolving to an unexpected scope, causing bugs that are hard to trace.
tiers.paperLevel: Scope defines the accessibility of variables and functions to various parts of the code. It has no single formula; it is a language-level rule set.

explainer.example: A variable declared inside a function is only visible within that function, so code outside it cannot read or change that variable.
